activity_context.topic_title: Solving Cubic Equations With Complex Roots

feedback.problem: Find all of the solutions to $2{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+20x-8=0$ given that $x=2-2\text{i}$ is a solution.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(x)=2{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+20x-8.$ 

Since $f(x)$ has real coefficients and ${x}_{1}=2-2\text{i}$ is a root of $f(x),$ the complex conjugate 

$$
\overset{―}{{x}_{1}}=\overset{―}{2-2\text{i}}=2+2\text{i}
$$

must also be a root of $f(x).$

Now, according to the factor theorem, 
$(x-(2-2\text{i}))(x-(2+2\text{i}))$
is a factor of $f(x).$ Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-(2-2\text{i}))(x-(2+2\text{i})) & = \\ {x}^{2}-(2-2\text{i}+2+2\text{i})x+(2-2\text{i})(2+2\text{i}) & = \\ {x}^{2}-4x+({2}^{2}-(2\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ {x}^{2}-4x+8 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by ${x}^{2}-4x+8$ using polynomial division.

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,\,2x-1 \\  & {x}^{2}-4x+8\,\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,2{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+20x-8\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{2{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+16x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,-{x}^{2}+4x-8 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,{x}^{2}+4x-8}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $f(x)=({x}^{2}-4x+8)(2x-1).$ 

To find the remaining root, we set the linear factor equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-1=0\,⟹\,x=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the roots are $x=\frac{1}{2},2\pm 2\text{i}.$
